newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - CE would build up N.Elec.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - CE would build up N.Elec.

text.p: U.S. energy group CalEnergy intends to build the business of British regional electricity company (Rec) Northern Electric and expand abroad if its $1.225 billion takeover bid is successful, chairman David Sokol said.
"Our intention is to build this business, not to try and strip it," he told Reuters in an interview.
"We intend to expand the business (overseas), we intend to do that out of Newcastle," he added.
CalEnergy made the 630 pence per share offer through its 70 percent-owned unit CE Electric and has bought over 29 percent of Northern Electric, based in Newcastle, north east England.
But Northern has rejected the bid as undervaluing the company and promised to rush out interim results by the end of the month to help show its higher value.
Sokol said he saw good synergies between the two companies.
In electricity supply, Sokol said CalEnergy would bring "a better entrepeneurial vision...we know how to buy and sell electricity."

He said Northern had done a "credible job" moving into supply but that liberalisation of the market in 1998 would require aggressive marketing, strong infrastructure to cut delivery costs and buying at the lowest price.
CalEnergy is the largest environmental generator in the U.S. but lacks distribution assets.
Sokol said CalEnergy would be able to introduce Northern into international market which need distribution skills.
"It is a very synergistic fit of talents," he said.
Sokol said Northern was more attractive than other Recs because it had the synergies but was also smaller.
He said if the takeover went ahead, CalEnergy did not envisage any job losses on top of those already planned by Northern. "We are looking at...turning the business international," he added.
Sokol said that expansion in the UK might involve moving into other markets, bundling other services such as telecommunications, media and information services.
But he said any move into telecoms would most likely be through a joint venture rather than an acqusition.

He said Northern's stake in Ionica, a radio-based telephony company, was likely to be sold if CalEnergy secured control of Northern. "We would either sell or continue to fund (it) until it was sellable," he said.
The bid also awaits approval from UK competition authorities.
